title: 1100 AI Employees Jointly Appeal to Washington: It's Time to Slow Down AI Development

content_html:
According to Business Insider, more than 1,100 employees from leading AI companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have signed an open letter calling on the U.S. government to slow down the development of AI. This initiative, named "Controlling the Frontier," directly addresses the serious lag in safety and governance systems in the current AI arms race. The open letter focuses on the core issue of "automated AI development"—the ability of future AI to autonomously develop and improve AI systems through "recursive self-improvement." Anthropic has stated that its Claude series models are rapidly approaching this threshold. The letter warns that the development of AI capabilities may accelerate quickly beyond human ability to understand or control these systems, and calls on the U.S. government to support international cooperation to develop necessary technologies and governance tools, consciously controlling the progress of automated AI development.

Executive Backing, Altman's Shift in Stance

The list of signatories of this open letter can be considered an "all-star" lineup in the AI industry—Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, along with two co-founders, Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI, Shengjia Zhao, Chief Scientist at Meta, and Anca Dragan, Head of AI Safety and Alignment Work at Google DeepMind, are all included. OpenAI and Anthropic subsequently posted messages on X platform in support; the former acknowledged that at some point in the future, the acceleration of frontier model development might become so fast that the world needs to slow down, while the latter cited its research on recursive self-improvement released last month, emphasizing the need for society to have time to prepare.

Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, showed a particularly notable shift in stance. In an interview with the "Invest Like the Best" podcast, he said it might now be time to "slow down" the pace of AI development, allowing society to adapt to new capabilities and establish protective mechanisms.

However, he also emphasized that this approach should not be perceived as regulatory capture or collusion among leading laboratories. Just a year ago, when faced with an open letter advocating a similar "slowing down AI development" proposal, Altman had refused to sign, citing a lack of key technical details. From avoiding signing in 2023 to now publicly supporting it, this change itself reflects a deep transformation in the AI industry's perception of safety risks.

content_html_zh:
据 Business Insider 报道，来自 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、Meta 等领先 AI 公司的 1100 多名员工签署了一封公开信，呼吁美国政府放慢 AI 的发展速度。 这一名为“控制前沿”的举措直接解决了当前人工智能军备竞赛中安全和治理系统严重滞后的问题。 公开信聚焦“人工智能自动化开发”的核心问题——未来人工智能通过“递归自我完善”自主开发和改进人工智能系统的能力。 Anthropic表示，其Claude系列型号正在迅速逼近这一门槛。 信中警告说，人工智能能力的发展可能会迅速加速，超出人类理解或控制这些系统的能力，并呼吁美国政府支持国际合作，开发必要的技术和治理工具，有意识地控制自动化人工智能发展的进度。

高管支持，奥特曼立场转变

这封公开信的签署者名单堪称AI行业的“全明星”阵容——Anthropic首席执行官Dario Amodei以及两位联合创始人OpenAI首席科学家Jakub Pachocki、Meta首席科学家赵胜佳、Google DeepMind人工智能安全与对齐工作负责人Anca Dragan都在其中。 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 随后在 X 平台上发布消息表示支持；前者承认，在未来的某个时刻，前沿模型发展的加速可能会变得如此之快，以至于世界需要放慢速度，而后者则引用了其上个月发布的关于递归自我改进的研究，强调社会需要有时间做好准备。

OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 的立场发生了特别显着的转变。 他在接受“Invest Like the Best”播客采访时表示，现在可能是时候“放慢”人工智能发展的步伐，让社会适应新的能力并建立保护机制。

不过，他也强调，这种做法不应被视为监管捕获或领先实验室之间的勾结。 就在一年前，当面对一封提倡类似“放慢人工智能发展”提案的公开信时，奥特曼以缺乏关键技术细节为由拒绝签署。 从2023年避免签署到现在公开支持，这一变化本身就体现了AI行业对安全风险认知的深刻转变。
